steps.what: Prepare discussion questions grounded in the actual lesson

loop.purpose: Suggest candidate prompts from the teacher's lesson
loop.check: Teacher checks factual premises, relevance, sensitive assumptions and whether questions invite useful discussion
loop.stop: Missing lesson support or two failed drafts returns prompt writing to the teacher
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed question structure is tried first; open-ended family and consumer issues need contextual wording

steps.what: Initiate, facilitate and moderate the actual classroom discussion

tasks.design: Try a native question outline in {DOCS}, then use a bounded drafting loop only for candidate prompts grounded in the actual lesson. The teacher checks every prompt and retains the entire live discussion, including handling sensitive family or financial experiences.
tasks.previous_blocker: Wording suitable open questions takes preparation alongside live facilitation.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bound candidate drafting with full teacher selection.
tasks.still_hard: Managing participation, disagreement and sensitive disclosures in real time.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the discussion requires a different question or a supportive intervention.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less prompt drafting, without changing classroom responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source-bound candidate question drafting can support lesson preparation, while actual discussion moderation remains human.

assumptions: Provisional shares describe a lesson with actual written discussion prompts. A spontaneous discussion without preparation must remove and reweight s1.
The teacher supplies lesson extracts, objective and topic boundaries in s1; obtaining and selecting these inputs is retained there. No student profiling or emotional inference is used.
Native question outlines are tested first. The three removed points cover candidate wording only; source selection, sensitive-topic review and live moderation remain.

Record and send boundaries were inspected: this task does not require a new class-progress record or outward message. The actual written artefact is the prompt set in s1, with its ordinary save retained.
unknowns: Actual amount of prompt writing before discussion
research_questions: Do candidate prompts reduce actual wording work after the teacher's relevance and sensitivity check?

incremental.description: Maintain lesson boundaries and review candidate quality

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 15 times 20%=3 wording points less 0.6 upkeep gives 2.4. With sensitive family topics, the teacher rewrites most questions; only 1 point of neutral prompt wording disappears, giving 0.4 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Revise family and consumer sciences curricula

steps.what: Review learning evidence and current subject and curriculum requirements
Choose course progression, content changes and teaching methods
Write revised lessons, practical activities and course content
Apply repeated course layout and insert verified course metadata
Check the complete revision and save the internal course version

tasks.design: Test native {DOCS} styles and course templates, then assemble repeated layout from teacher-authored revisions. Keep evaluation, pedagogy, practical-activity design and complete final checking human; only actual repeated formatting is removed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual layout work accompanies substantive course revision.
tasks.enabler_now: Native styles and deterministic document assembly.
tasks.still_hard: Connecting family, finance, nutrition and practical learning into a coherent curriculum.
tasks.human_edge: Choose teaching methods appropriate to the actual learners and subject evidence.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated layout, without new curriculum authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: document assembly can apply repeated structure to teacher-written content without evaluating teaching methods.

assumptions: Provisional shares end at an internally checked course revision. Actual committee adoption or student publication must be separately modelled where assigned.

Course administration provides course code, version and required sections. s1 verifies these as checked course metadata; s2 decides revisions and s3 writes all substantive content. Missing requirements require manual clarification.

Native styles are tested before custom assembly. Ten points represent manual layout that still exists today, excluding already automatic formatting. Full final checks and ordinary ungated save remain.
unknowns: Reusable template availability for practical lessons
research_questions: Which layout interactions remain manual after native styles are used?

incremental.description: Maintain course layouts and metadata mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 10 layout points less 1 upkeep gives 9. A new practical nutrition course needs bespoke activity pages, leaving only 1.8 points of reusable course metadata placement and 0.8 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Compile the examination and check questions against learning outcomes
Administer the actual examination and handle student or delivery issues
Mark closed examination answers against the checked key
Grade open answers and resolve ambiguous or invalid items
Check all results and authorise the final student result release
Release the exact authorised examination results to the specified students

tasks.design: Configure the existing examination tools in {LMS} for reusable question layout and exact closed-answer marking. Retain question validity, examination administration, every open-answer judgement and complete result checks, followed by a separate gated formal result release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Question layout and fixed-key marking can remain manual.
tasks.enabler_now: Native item banks and deterministic closed-question marking.
tasks.still_hard: Valid assessment of practical reasoning and ambiguous student answers.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether an answer demonstrates understanding and whether an item was fair.
tasks.altitude: Less fixed-key marking, retaining examiner authority.

evidence.claim: Ans supports closed-question marking and item statistics; no AI is needed for fixed answer keys.

assumptions: Provisional shares represent an examiner personally compiling and marking a mixed examination; assistants' work is not counted as saved. Existing automatic marking must be removed from the baseline.

s1 supplies exact item identifiers, key, rubric and checked exam version, including their manual creation and validation. s2 creates actual submissions with student and item identifiers. Missing or ambiguous responses go to s4.
Test native configuration first. Three s1 points concern reused question layout, not new question content. s3 removes only fixed-key marking. No AI grading or cheating inference is used.

s5 authorises formal release only after the complete result set exists; changes void approval. This is a student result decision, not an ordinary author save. Registry double entry belongs to the separate records task and must not be added twice.
unknowns: Actual mix of closed and open questions
research_questions: How much fixed-key marking is still manual for this examination?

incremental.description: Maintain item mappings and validate changed keys

approvals.approved_version: s5 exact exam version, student-result set and release audience; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 3 reused-layout points plus 20 fixed-key points=23, less 1 upkeep gives 22. An essay-heavy examination leaves only 1 reusable-layout point and 4 fixed-key marking points removable, giving 4 net; all open judgement remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain attendance, grades and required student records

steps.what: Capture actual attendance and required student record facts
Verify captured facts and final examiner-set grades
Enter the verified facts into the learning-system record
Check and authorise the final registry transfer and destination
Re-enter the authorised grade data into the separate student registry
Check the transfer receipt and retain its record reference

tasks.design: Test the native export/import between {LMS} and the student registry represented by {OTHER}, then transfer the exact authorised results without re-keying. Keep actual attendance capture, grade verification, initial record entry and final transfer checks human; the gated action writes into a genuinely separate registry.
tasks.previous_blocker: Final grades can require duplicate entry in a separate official registry.
tasks.enabler_now: A controlled structured result import with exact student and course mappings.
tasks.still_hard: Identity mismatches, exceptional grade scales and resolving incomplete records.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve discrepancies without changing a student's result by inference.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate registry entry, with examiner responsibility unchanged.

evidence.claim: Radboud's Brightspace grades must also be published in OSIRIS, documenting a real separate-registry entry boundary.

assumptions: Provisional shares assume this institution has actual duplicate grade entry; the digest establishes an example, not this customer's baseline. Existing automatic transfers earn no saving.

s1 captures attendance and other actual events. The marking process produces examiner-set grades outside this records task; no grading labour is claimed here. s2 verifies student identifier, course, attempt, grade scale, value and status against the roster; missing identifiers require manual resolution.

s3 creates the exact complete source record before s4 authorises the mapped transfer snapshot and target. Native supported import is tested first. s5 re-keys into a distinct registry today; it is not a same-system save.

Failed mappings remain manual within retained verification/check work; if their volume exceeds that allowance, increase retained work and reduce the benefit. Changes after s4 void transfer approval. Ordinary receipt saves remain retained and ungated.
unknowns: Whether a separate official registry is used
research_questions: Measure actual duplicate entry and test student/course/attempt mappings on a real authorised batch.

incremental.description: Maintain registry field and grade-scale mappings

approvals.approved_version: s4 exact student/course/attempt result snapshot, mapping version and target registry; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 25 duplicate-entry points less 1 upkeep gives 24. With exceptional attempts and mixed grade scales, only 5 points of fully mapped records transfer automatically; retain all exception re-keying and checks, giving 4 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain discussion, curriculum and examiner decisions while reducing actual formatting, fixed-key marking and distinct-registry re-entry.
skills_to_grow: Check discussion prompts for sensitive assumptions
role.ambitious_version: Use verified recovered time for student explanation and practical course design.
